Mei HaShiloach distinguishes expansion in unholy desires from Yaakov's expansion in holiness

Rambam asked how a person’s choice can be free if Hashem knows beforehand whether he will be righteous or wicked, and answered that His knowledge is not like ours (Hilchot Teshuvah 5:5; see note 282 below). Rav Tzadok holds that this admission is itself the true answer, and he explains it, after Tikkunei Zohar Chadash and the Ari’s Arba Me’ot Shekel Kesef, as two truths that stand in two different “places”: “In the place of knowledge there is no choice, and in the place of choice there is no grasp of His knowledge; choice exists only from the side of this world” (Takanat HaShavin 6). The place of knowledge is hidden in this world and will be revealed in the future, when the evil inclination is removed and choice falls away (Machshavot Charutz 8; Resisei Layla 50). Elsewhere he spells out that this is Rambam’s answer itself: for us two opposites cannot rest in one subject, but for Hashem they can (citing Maharal’s introduction to Gevurot Hashem); “for us there is choice, and for Hashem knowledge,” and when we merit such a revelation of Godliness that “the righteous will be called by the name of the Holy One” (Bava Batra 75b), we will see that there was no room for choice at all (Likkutei Maamarim, On Shimshon 17)
